issues.title: Dataframe-wide integer coercion still silently wraps overflowing values
issues.body:
Bug
The integer overflow protection introduced in #2443 still allows wraparound when the dtype is set on the entire DataFrameSchema.
import pandas as pd
import pandera.pandas as pa

pa.DataFrameSchema(dtype="int8", coerce=True).validate(pd.DataFrame({"a": [300]}))
# validated dataframe contains 44

pa.DataFrameSchema(dtype="uint8", coerce=True).validate(pd.DataFrame({"a": [-1]}))
# validated dataframe contains 255
The analogous per-column schemas reject these inputs. A dataframe has dtypes, not a single dtype, so _check_integer_overflow returns early when handed the whole frame.
I reproduced this on current main and prepared a focused fix that applies the existing check to each dataframe column by position (also covering duplicate column names). Tests cover four target dtypes and eager/lazy schema validation, plus duplicate names through the dtype coercion API, valid casts, and empty-frame controls. Duplicate-name schema error formatting has a separate existing TypeError and is not changed here. I intend to contribute the fix.
AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation and this report.

issues.body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Sensor and event data often need two checks that today require custom code: that a timestamp column or index is in order, and that consecutive readings are never further apart than the expected reporting interval. For example, a water-quality sensor should report every 5 minutes, so a 30-minute gap means missing data. Check.is_monotonic exists for xarray coordinates, but it takes a dim argument and isn't available for pandas or polars columns.

Two built-in checks:

Check.is_sorted(ascending=True, strict=False): each value is compared with the previous non-null value; strict=True also rejects repeated values.

issues.title: Feature request: support Pydantic v2-style model_config: ConfigDict in addition to nested class Config
issues.body:
Pandera's DataFrameModel currently only supports schema-wide configuration via a nested class literally named Config:
class MyModel(pa.DataFrameModel):
    x: float
    y: float

    class Config:
        coerce = True
        strict = True

This mirrors Pydantic v1's config style. Since Pydantic v2 moved to an explicit, typed model_config class attribute:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class MyModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(coerce=True, strict=True)

    x: float
    y: float


...it would be great if pandera.DataFrameModel supported an analogous pattern, e.g.:
from pandera import DataFrameConfigDict

class MyModel(pa.DataFrameModel):
    model_config: DataFrameConfigDict = DataFrameConfigDict(coerce=True, strict=True)

    x: float
    y: float


Motivation:
Codebases that mix Pydantic v2 models and pandera DataFrameModels currently have two different config conventions side by side, which is a small but recurring friction point.
A typed ConfigDict-style object would let static type checkers (Pyright/mypy) validate config keys and value types at definition time, catching typos immediately — right now, an unrecognized attribute on class Config (e.g. a misspelled option name) can silently be interpreted as a registered dataframe check rather than raising a clear error, which is a confusing failure mode to debug.
It would bring the class-based API closer to parity with Pydantic's ergonomics, which pandera already draws heavy inspiration from.

issues.title: Perplexity returns infinity for uniform float16 logits
issues.body:
🐛 Bug description
Perplexity sums cross-entropy in the logits' dtype. With float16 logits, the total negative log-likelihood can overflow even when the mean loss and expected perplexity are small.
import torch
from ignite.metrics.nlp import Perplexity

torch.set_num_threads(1)
metric = Perplexity()
logits = torch.zeros(32, 16, 1024, dtype=torch.float16)
targets = torch.zeros(32, 1024, dtype=torch.long)
metric.update((logits, targets))

The same example with bfloat16 returns approximately 15.889. Splitting the float16 inputs into batches of four avoids infinity but returns approximately 16.108 on this CPU environment.
A proposed fix is to compute cross-entropy in float32 when logits are float16 or bfloat16, retaining the existing float32/float64 paths. An exact uniform-distribution oracle can cover both overflow and batch partitioning, with additional checks for ignored tokens and float64 logits.

issues.title: New semantics of blockSignal in Parameter.setValue() suppresses ParameterItem updates
issues.body:
The PR #3305 changes Parameter.setValue() such that setting blockSignal prevents sigValueChanged from being emitted.
That silently breaks the old blockSignal=callable pattern, used both in user code and in pyqtgraph's own examples/parametertree.py.
Previously, blockSignal was used to specify a single slot to ignore during the value update. When a parameter was supposed to reflect a model value, blockSignal could help prevent recursion while still allowing corresponding ParameterItems to display updated values.

        super().__init__()
        self.on = False

        self.on = on
        self.sigSwitched.emit(self.on)


class MainWindow(QWidget):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

        self.param = Parameter.create(name='param', type='bool', value=False)
        paramTree = ParameterTree(self)
        paramTree.addParameters(self.param)
        toggleButton = QPushButton('toggle light')

        layout = QVBoxLayout()
        layout.addWidget(paramTree)
        layout.addWidget(toggleButton)
        self.setLayout(layout)

issues.title: Server gateway: reconnect `stream.events` with `since` after a mid turn drop
issues.body:
On a turn that sends a new message, LangGraphServerGateway pumps thread.stream().events. If that SSE ends before a root lifecycle stop, the gateway raises and cancels through the existing error path (#700). A better recovery is to reopen the stream with since=<last event id> and continue the same run without cancelling.
Scope: path for a new message only until resume work in #706 decides whether subscribe needs the same. Needs a real langgraph dev drop probe and a fake that can restart mid queue. Related: #700, #706.

issues.title: Server gateway: long thread `stream.events` replay exceeds skip budget
issues.body:
With gateway_backend_serve: langgraph_server, each turn that sends a new message may call _ThreadEvents.skip_replay before run.start. On the inmem runtime the thread SSE replays all stored envelopes first, so skip time grows roughly linearly with prior turns. Around 150 to 200 turns the skip reaches the 30s cap and the turn ends with an error, so the run is never started on a connection that would miss live events.
Later work to consider: a server side replay complete signal, opening the SSE with a cursor, or binding turns that send a new message to a per run stream when the API allows it. Related: #700 (skip heuristics and cap), #706 (resume / since).

issues.title: Server gateway: detect lost live events after `stream.events` goes quiet
issues.body:
After #700, a turn that sends a new message on LangGraphServerGateway opens stream.events, optionally skips replay, then starts the run and pumps envelopes. If the skip quiet window ends while history is still replaying, or the SSE drops without a root lifecycle stop, the turn can wait until the client gives up. The 30s cap applies only while skipping replay.
Add a run level watchdog that polls client.runs.get(thread_id, run_id) while the pump waits. When the run status is terminal (error, success, timeout, interrupted) and no matching live envelope arrives within about 2 seconds, raise RuntimeError("Lost the run's live events") so the existing error path cancels and surfaces. Keep polling while status is pending or running. Pause delivery through input.requested / stream.interrupted must keep working. Cover with fakes and a real langgraph dev hang probe. Keep resume on subscribe as it is on main until #706.

issues.title: langgraph dev keeps running after Ctrl+C during startup
issues.body:
Describe the bug
Pressing Ctrl+C while langgraph dev is still starting leaves the server running in the background. start_langgraph_dev() spawns it in its own session, so the terminal's Ctrl+C reaches only the CLI. The callers (EvoSci deploy, EvoSci serve, and the CLI through ensure_langgraph_dev()) register their cleanup only after start_langgraph_dev() returns, and its health wait (up to 60 s) has no cleanup of its own. The server keeps the port, and its PID file and workspace sidecar stay on disk.
Afterwards, EvoSci deploy refuses because the port is already serving a langgraph dev; EvoSci / EvoSci serve in the same workspace reuse the leftover server and never stop it; in another workspace they report a workspace mismatch until EvoSci server stop is run.
To Reproduce

Run EvoSci deploy.
Press Ctrl+C while the server is still starting (before the ready banner).
Run EvoSci server status: the server is still running.

Expected behavior
Interrupting the startup stops the half-started server and removes its PID file and sidecar, as a Ctrl+C after startup does.
Additional context
POSIX today. On Windows the same applies once langgraph dev is started in its own process group. A fix in one place covers every caller: in start_langgraph_dev(), wrap everything after Popen (PID file, sidecar, _PROCESS and the health loop) in try: ... except BaseException: stop_langgraph_dev(proc); raise.
System information

OS: macOS 26.6
Python version: 3.13
EvoScientist version: 0.3.3

issues.title: Detach run_in_background jobs from the langgraph dev server so they survive a backend restart
issues.body:
The switch waits for idle using only the thread status (busy/interrupted), so it ignores run_in_background processes (related: #443), although they are children of the LG dev server, and stop_langgraph_dev terminates all of them.
So in the scenario where an agent starts a 2-hour training run in the background, the turn ends (so the thread is idle) and the user switches workspaces, the probe sees idle, the backend restarts, and the training run is killed.
The close path has the same gap since backend_has_active_runs returns False so there's no confirmation dialog.
We already have some tools in place as we serve get_bg_process_status, so we should either:

Add a GET /bg_processes/running (or count) route next to the existing one and include it in this function as a third "active" condition, so the switch waits for it and close uses it to confirm with the user.
Keep the probe as is, but make the switch and close dialogs name the running bg processes and ask the user before killing them.

Either option has implications for the UX though, since the user probably wants to keep these tasks running while working on a different workspace. (Could we detach them and not kill on exit?)
